newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dampier pipeline is not a firesale, govt says.
newsitem.headline: Dampier pipeline is not a firesale, govt says.

text.p: The state government of Western Australia said on Thursday that it expected competitive bidding for the 1,540 kilometre Dampier to Bunbury Natural Gas Pipeline (DBNGP) which it planned to privatise by the end of the year.
"It currently has a book value of $A1,050 million and it has about $A950 million of real debt still attached to it," state energy minister Colin Barnett told reporters.

"I would expect it is going to be an attractive asset and will get high bids but it's not a firesale. If we don't get bids that recover its value and repay the debt then it won't be sold," Barnett said.

He told a business luncheon earlier on Thursday that a cap on tariffs would be introduced for the first two years of operation under private ownership to ensure transport costs decine from around $A1.25 per gigajoule at present to around $A1 per gigajoule by the year 2000.
The pipeline transports gas from the North West Shelf to residential and business consumers in the southwest corner of Western Australia.
Current capacity is 500 terajoules a day.

The North West Shelf is an equal partnership between operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, Chevron Corp and the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
MiMi is a partnership between Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp.
